text:
Lady and measure share one thread,
“Margaret” is a feminine name — hence Lady.
“Thatcher” phonetically echoes “thatch”, but the deeper play is on the word “tacher” / “teacher” sound and measure — and more sharply, on the title “The Iron Lady.” The line hints at the merging of identity and title — woman + metaphor.
But the key layer is simpler and more elegant:
“Lady” directly references her widely used epithet Iron Lady — the defining label of her political persona.
Firm the helm where angels dread.
This is a cryptic twist on the phrase:
“Fools rush in where angels fear to tread.”
The line replaces “fools rush in” with firm the helm — suggesting uncompromising leadership and steely resolve. It implies decisiveness where others hesitate — a core perception of her political style.

7. Two letters mirror East and West,
A family name outlives the rest.
